extracted.intended_audience: USPTO managers, policymakers, stakeholders, and customers of patent and trademark services
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's FY1999/FY2000 business goals, performance measures, system modernization plans, customer-service targets, and legislative/operational changes affecting patent and trademark processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality legal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of registrability will be accurately and clearly stated throughout the examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed as a specific FY2000 goal: examiners must provide clear, accurate legal findings during every stage of examination so customers understand registrability decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely processing of trademark applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration will be determined within thirteen months of filing, and PTO notices will be issued in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-action pendency and overall timeliness are explicit targets; the Office plans to obtain and maintain staff/resources necessary to reach the first-action pendency goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of trademark products and official notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Care will be taken so that notices with the correct information will be issued (e.g., Filing receipts, Notice of Allowance, Notice of Abandonment, Certificates of Registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy of issued documents is a measurable product-quality objective; errors and incorrect information must be reduced via process improvements and root-cause analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective handling of customer concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Only clear and accurate answers will be provided to customer questions regarding problems or delays in the processing of trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A customer‑facing service standard: managers/staff must ensure responses resolve issues promptly and accurately; part of a broader program pairing managers and customers to solve service problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer satisfaction improvement and target
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall customer satisfaction (was 63% in FY1998, 69% in FY1999) with a FY1999 target of 80%; focus on timeliness and handling of delays/mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey results drive priority setting; improvements should be measured by customer surveys and targeted operational changes addressing top complaint areas (timeliness, delays, mistakes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measures from the customer's point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop performance measures that will assess the quality of employee work from the customers' point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers and customers will work together to solve and then improve service problems; specific staff assigned to find root causes of delays and errors; measures should reflect customer experience, not only internal metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement Trademark Law Treaty (TLT) provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement the provisions of the Trademark Law Treaty to simplify and harmonize filing/registration requirements and support multi-class and service mark registrations, while recognizing increased post-registration filing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational changes (systems and processes) must be made to comply with TLT; implementation is an explicit PTO priority for FY2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace paper with full electronic processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and deploy systems (TradeUps, TRAM, TEAS, TARR, TESS) to replace paper applications and permit full electronic processing of applications and related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roadmap: TradeUps enhancements (image and text editing, interface to e-TEAS), TRAM replacement with open systems, TEAS secure payment and submission, and TESS search engine upgrades; objective is end-to-end electronic filing, processing, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase number and types of electronic filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the number and types of applications filed electronically and expand online payment options (e.g., TEAS credit card payments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure uptake of TEAS (e.g., >20,000 filings in FY1999), decrease paper processing, and expand electronic acceptance in other systems (PTAS, OEMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize internal systems to enable technology use
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue restructuring internal systems to enable full use of technology and replacement of proprietary technologies with open systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes improving reporting capabilities, integrating intent-to-use processing, supporting workflow changes, and developing an open trademark information system starting in 2002; supports other goals like timeliness and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase accessibility and dissemination of IP information
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver information when and where customers need it, in the required format, and at an affordable price that covers costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a diverse dissemination program, use the Internet for ordering and delivery, improve accessibility across U.S. regions (PTDLs, Partnership Libraries), and contain dissemination costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand online ordering, delivery, and document services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide online ordering and around-the-clock document ordering (OEMS), allow customers to check order status and receive patents/electronic products online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEMS must provide secure credit-card processing, multiple pricing/delivery options, and electronic delivery where feasible; PTAS upgrades to accept electronic/fax requests and future Internet submission/recordation are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage information technology for operational improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use IT to improve funds processing (e.g., POS check conversion), expand secure online payments, provide continuous online services, and support the electronic workplace vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IT investments should improve cash forecasting, reduce processing time, reduce fraud risk, enable remote work, and increase customers' self‑service capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-at-home program expansion to increase productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand successful Work-at-Home pilot (which increased productivity for participating examiners) to more examining attorneys as an alternative method for addressing increasing filings and limited office space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot results support rollout to up to 60 examiners and potential further expansion; remote work is an operational lever to meet service demand without additional physical space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and maintain staff and resources to meet goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire and retain necessary staff and resources to reach first-action pendency and other service goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human-resources planning and funding are explicitly tied to achieving timeliness, quality, and electronic-processing targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management and accountability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain accurate financial data, achieve unqualified audit opinions, correct internal control deficiencies, and manage Fund Balance with Treasury responsibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue modernization of financial management systems, link accounting with budgeting for better decision-making, and address restrictions on fund balances to ensure long-term mission capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase number of registrations published and registered
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase throughput so that more trademark registrations are published and registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through operational efficiency, electronic filing, staffing, and process reforms, the Office aims to raise the registration publication and grant rates.
